evals.name: pdf-tools-workdir
evals.prompt: I want to build an MCP server that wraps our internal PDF handling so Claude can pull page counts and extract the text from PDFs sitting in a shared folder. Set it up so it runs in Docker, and I want to be able to test it without spinning up the whole thing.
evals.expected_output: A complete runnable project: server module with pypdf-backed tools confined to one mounted directory, http entrypoint, healthcheck, in-process test script, Dockerfile, docker-compose with a test profile. Uses mcp SDK v2 (MCPServer), transport args on run(), pypdf in requirements.
assertions: Transport and networking arguments are passed to mcp.run(), not to the MCPServer constructor
Compose has a profile-gated test service, so a plain `up` does not run the tests
Dockerfile COPYs every runnable file that a compose service invokes, including the test script
Test script checks is_error on a deliberately bad call instead of expecting a raised exception
Healthcheck checks that the TCP port accepts a connection rather than making an HTTP GET to /mcp
Every tool has a docstring that says what each parameter does, not only what the tool does
Tools raise ToolError from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions, so the failure message actually reaches the model instead of being replaced by "Error executing tool <name>"
The test asserts on the error message text, not only on is_error, so a swallowed message is caught
The MCPServer instructions argument is filled in with real guidance, not left as a TODO
File access is confined to one directory: paths are resolved and anything outside is refused
Compose mounts the shared PDF folder as a host volume, so files on the host are visible to the tools
Provides a page-count tool and a text-extraction tool, both with typed return values

evals.name: github-api-no-workdir
evals.prompt: set up an mcp server that hits the github rest api - i want tools to list my open PRs and get the diff for one of them. needs to run in docker. no idea what the current python sdk looks like
evals.expected_output: A complete runnable project with no filesystem working directory or volume mount, httpx in requirements, a token read from the environment, tools with clear docstrings, and the same container/test scaffolding. Uses mcp SDK v2 (MCPServer, not FastMCP).
assertions: Transport and networking arguments are passed to mcp.run(), not to the MCPServer constructor
Compose has a profile-gated test service, so a plain `up` does not run the tests
Dockerfile COPYs every runnable file that a compose service invokes, including the test script
Test script checks is_error on a deliberately bad call instead of expecting a raised exception
Healthcheck checks that the TCP port accepts a connection rather than making an HTTP GET to /mcp
Every tool has a docstring that says what each parameter does, not only what the tool does
Tools raise ToolError from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions, so the failure message actually reaches the model instead of being replaced by "Error executing tool <name>"
The test asserts on the error message text, not only on is_error, so a swallowed message is caught
The MCPServer instructions argument is filled in with real guidance, not left as a TODO
No filesystem working directory and no volume mount, since the server wraps an API
The GitHub token is read from an environment variable and never hardcoded
Provides a tool to list open pull requests and a tool to fetch one pull request's diff

evals.name: terse-boilerplate
evals.prompt: give me a starter mcp server skeleton in python, docker, with a test i can actually run
evals.expected_output: A runnable scaffold whose example tools work out of the box, so the test passes before any domain code is written. Includes Dockerfile, docker-compose with a test profile, and a README with the commands.
assertions: Transport and networking arguments are passed to mcp.run(), not to the MCPServer constructor
Compose has a profile-gated test service, so a plain `up` does not run the tests
Dockerfile COPYs every runnable file that a compose service invokes, including the test script
Test script checks is_error on a deliberately bad call instead of expecting a raised exception
Healthcheck checks that the TCP port accepts a connection rather than making an HTTP GET to /mcp
Every tool has a docstring that says what each parameter does, not only what the tool does
Tools raise ToolError from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions, so the failure message actually reaches the model instead of being replaced by "Error executing tool <name>"
The test asserts on the error message text, not only on is_error, so a swallowed message is caught

notes: Eight assertions were dropped after iteration 1 because both configurations passed them in every run, so they measured the model's own MCP knowledge rather than the skill. Kept despite being non-discriminating in iteration 1: path confinement and the environment-read token, because they guard security properties worth catching a regression on, and the volume-mount checks, because they test the skill's own workdir vs no-workdir branch.
